board_events.text: A particle moves anticlockwise on a circle of radius $A$ at constant $\omega$; at time $t$ its radius makes angle $(\omega t+\phi)$.
So the shadow on the $x$-axis is SHM with amplitude $A$ and angular frequency $\omega$.
The centripetal acceleration $\omega^2 A$ projects to the SHM acceleration $\omega^2 x$.
The two perpendicular projections are themselves SHMs, ninety degrees out of phase.

segments.text: Let us prove the reference-circle claim properly, because it is the backbone of the phasor method that follows.
The picture is the setup: a bead circling at constant speed, with its position projected onto both axes by the dashed lines.
Set it up carefully. A particle moves anticlockwise on a circle of radius A at constant angular speed omega. At time t its radius makes an angle omega t plus phi with the x-axis.
Its coordinates are then x equals A cosine of omega t plus phi, and y equals A sine of the same angle. Those are the two projections, onto the horizontal and vertical axes.

Now differentiate the x-projection twice. The first derivative brings a sine and a factor omega; the second brings back a cosine with omega squared and a minus sign, giving minus omega squared A cosine, which is just minus omega squared x.
That is the S H M equation exactly. So the shadow on the x-axis is simple harmonic motion, with amplitude equal to the radius A and angular frequency equal to the circulation rate omega.

<excited>And the geometry is lovely. The centripetal acceleration of the circular motion, omega squared A pointing to the centre, projects onto the axis as the S H M acceleration, omega squared x. The circular speed omega A likewise projects to the S H M speed.
One bonus: the two perpendicular projections, the x and the y, are each simple harmonic motions, and they are ninety degrees out of phase, one a cosine and the other a sine.
चलो reference-circle claim को ठीक से prove करें, क्योंकि यही आगे आने वाले phasor method की रीढ़ है.
picture setup है: एक bead constant speed पर घूमता, dashed lines से इसकी position दोनों axes पर projected.
इसे ध्यान से set करो. एक particle radius A के circle पर constant angular speed omega पर anticlockwise चलती है. time t पर इसका radius x-axis के साथ omega t plus phi angle बनाता है.
इसके coordinates फिर हैं x बराबर A cosine of omega t plus phi, और y बराबर उसी angle का A sine. वो दो projections हैं, horizontal और vertical axes पर.

<excited>अब x-projection को दो बार differentiate करो. पहला derivative एक sine और factor omega लाता है; दूसरा वापस एक cosine लाता है omega squared और minus sign के साथ, यानी minus omega squared A cosine, जो बस minus omega squared x है.
यही exactly S H M equation है. तो x-axis पर shadow simple harmonic motion है, amplitude बराबर radius A और angular frequency बराबर circulation rate omega के साथ.

और geometry प्यारी है. circular motion का centripetal acceleration, omega squared A centre की तरफ, axis पर S H M acceleration, omega squared x, के रूप में project होता है. circular speed omega A भी S H M speed में project होती है.
एक bonus: दोनों perpendicular projections, x और y, हर एक simple harmonic motions हैं, और वो ninety degrees out of phase हैं, एक cosine और दूसरी sine.

sections.subtopic: Reference Circle, Superposition and More SHM Systems
sections.title: Derivation: the phasor method for collinear SHMs

board_events.text: Two radius vectors at a fixed angle

board_events.caption: Two rotating radius vectors add like ordinary vectors

board_events.text: Represent $x_1=A_1\cos\omega t$ and $x_2=A_2\cos(\omega t+\delta)$ as two rotating radius vectors with fixed angle $\delta$.
Since both rotate at the same $\omega$, the angle between them never changes, so they add like ordinary vectors.
The resultant is again an SHM of the same frequency.
This is why a phasor diagram turns trigonometry into geometry.

segments.text: Now the phasor method, which turns a messy trig sum into a simple triangle. This is the everyday tool for adding two collinear oscillations.
The picture shows the idea: two arrows from the origin at a fixed angle, and their vector sum reaching out to the resultant.

Represent the first motion, x-one equals A-one cosine omega t, and the second, x-two equals A-two cosine of omega t plus delta, as two rotating radius vectors of lengths A-one and A-two, with a fixed angle delta between them.

Here is the crucial observation. Since both phasors rotate at the same omega, the angle between them never changes. A rigid pair of vectors rotating together can simply be added like ordinary vectors, once and for all.
The resultant length follows from the law of cosines, with the included angle delta: A is the square root of A-one squared plus A-two squared plus twice A-one A-two cosine delta.
And the resultant's phase comes from resolving into components: the tangent of phi is A-two sine delta, over A-one plus A-two cosine delta.
The resultant is again a simple harmonic motion of the very same frequency, just with a new amplitude and a new phase.
<chuckle>And that is the whole beauty of the phasor picture: it turns a trigonometric identity into a piece of triangle geometry, which is far easier to see and to trust.
अब phasor method, जो एक messy trig sum को एक simple triangle में बदल देता है. यही दो collinear oscillations जोड़ने का रोज़मर्रा का tool है.
picture idea दिखाती है: origin से दो arrows एक fixed angle पर, और इनका vector sum resultant तक पहुँचता हुआ.

पहली motion, x-one बराबर A-one cosine omega t, और दूसरी, x-two बराबर A-two cosine of omega t plus delta, को दो rotating radius vectors के रूप में represent करो, lengths A-one और A-two, बीच में fixed angle delta के साथ.

<chuckle>यही crucial observation है. चूँकि दोनों phasors same omega पर rotate करते हैं, इनके बीच का angle कभी नहीं बदलता. साथ घूमते vectors की एक rigid जोड़ी को बस ordinary vectors की तरह जोड़ा जा सकता है, हमेशा के लिए.
resultant length law of cosines से आती है, included angle delta के साथ: A है square root of A-one squared plus A-two squared plus twice A-one A-two cosine delta.
और resultant का phase components में resolve करने से आता है: phi का tangent है A-two sine delta, over A-one plus A-two cosine delta.
resultant फिर से उसी frequency का एक simple harmonic motion है, बस एक नई amplitude और नए phase के साथ.
और यही phasor picture की पूरी खूबसूरती है: ये एक trigonometric identity को triangle geometry के एक टुकड़े में बदल देती है, जो देखना और भरोसा करना कहीं आसान है.

board_events.text: U-tube: displacing $y$ makes a height difference $2y$. Float: extra buoyancy $A\rho g\,x$. Tunnel: gravity at depth is $g\,r/R$.
One method, every system: no memorised formula, just $\ddot{x}=-\omega^2 x$.

segments.text: Now the payoff of the universal test: three of the hardest-looking J E E systems, each collapsing to one line. The recipe is always the same.

Displace the system by a small amount, find the net restoring force or write its energy, force the result into the shape acceleration equals minus omega squared times displacement, and read omega straight off.
The picture shows all three side by side, with the restoring effect marked on each.

First the U-tube. Push the liquid down one arm by y and it rises y in the other, creating a height difference of two y. The unbalanced weight gives acceleration equals minus two g over L, times y, so the period is two pi root L over two g.

Next the floating body. Push it down by x and the extra submerged volume gives an extra buoyant force upward. The acceleration comes out as minus g over h, times x, so the period is two pi root h over g.

Then the tunnel through the Earth. For a uniform Earth, gravity at distance r from the centre is g times r over R, always pointing to the centre, so the acceleration is minus g over R, times r, and the period is two pi root R over g.

<curious>Notice what fed each one: for the U-tube, the doubled height difference two y; for the float, the extra buoyancy A rho g x; for the tunnel, gravity growing as g r over R. Different physics, identical shape.
So there is nothing to memorise here beyond one line. Displace, find the restoring acceleration, match it to minus omega squared x, and the period falls out. One method, every system.
अब universal test का फल: तीन सबसे मुश्किल-दिखने वाले J E E systems, हर एक एक line में सिमटता हुआ. recipe हमेशा वही है.
system को थोड़ा displace करो, net restoring force ढूँढो या energy लिखो, result को acceleration बराबर minus omega squared times displacement के shape में लाओ, और omega सीधे पढ़ लो.
picture तीनों को साथ दिखाती है, हर एक पर restoring effect marked.

पहले U-tube. liquid को एक arm में y से नीचे धकेलो तो दूसरे में y ऊपर उठता है, two y का height difference बनता है. unbalanced weight देता है acceleration बराबर minus two g over L, times y, तो period है two pi root L over two g.
<curious>फिर floating body. इसे x से नीचे धकेलो तो extra submerged volume एक extra buoyant force ऊपर देता है. acceleration निकलता है minus g over h, times x, तो period है two pi root h over g.
फिर Earth में tunnel. uniform Earth के लिए centre से r दूरी पर gravity है g times r over R, हमेशा centre की तरफ, तो acceleration है minus g over R, times r, और period है two pi root R over g.

ध्यान दो हर एक को क्या feed कर रहा था: U-tube के लिए दुगुना height difference two y; float के लिए extra buoyancy A rho g x; tunnel के लिए g r over R की तरह बढ़ती gravity. अलग physics, identical shape.
तो यहाँ एक line से आगे याद रखने को कुछ नहीं. displace करो, restoring acceleration ढूँढो, उसे minus omega squared x से match करो, और period निकल आता है. एक method, हर system.

sections.subtopic: Reference Circle, Superposition and More SHM Systems
sections.title: Worked example (CBSE): resultant of two collinear SHMs

board_events.text: Perpendicular phasors add by Pythagoras
Two SHMs act along the same line: $x_1=3\sin\omega t$ and $x_2=4\sin(\omega t+\pi/2)$ cm. Find the resultant amplitude and phase.

board_events.caption: The 3-4-5 right triangle is the phasor diagram itself

board_events.text: Perpendicular phasors add by Pythagoras, so the resultant is simply the hypotenuse.
Amplitude 5 cm at phase about 53 degrees: the classic 3-4-5 triangle.

segments.text: A clean C B S E example that lets the phasor method pay off immediately. Two simple harmonic motions act along the same line.
The first is three sine omega t centimetres, and the second is four sine of omega t plus pi over two centimetres. Find the amplitude and initial phase of the resultant motion.
The picture is the whole answer in disguise: a three-four-five right triangle, which is exactly the phasor diagram.
The phase difference is pi over two, so its cosine is zero. That is what makes the two phasors perpendicular, and it kills the cross term in the amplitude formula.
The resultant amplitude is the square root of three squared plus four squared plus zero, which is the root of twenty-five, exactly five centimetres.
The phase has tangent equal to four times one, over three plus zero, that is four over three, so phi is about fifty-three degrees.

<chuckle>Notice what happened. Because the phasors were perpendicular, they added by Pythagoras, and the resultant is simply the hypotenuse of the three-four-five triangle. No heavy trigonometry at all.
So the answer is an amplitude of five centimetres at a phase of about fifty-three degrees, the classic three-four-five triangle sitting quietly inside an oscillation problem.
एक साफ़ C B S E example जो phasor method को तुरंत काम दिखाने देता है. दो simple harmonic motions एक ही line के साथ act करती हैं.
पहली है three sine omega t centimetres, और दूसरी है four sine of omega t plus pi over two centimetres. resultant motion की amplitude और initial phase निकालो.
picture disguise में पूरा answer है: एक three-four-five right triangle, जो exactly phasor diagram है.
phase difference है pi over two, तो इसका cosine zero है. यही दोनों phasors को perpendicular बनाता है, और amplitude formula का cross term खत्म कर देता है.
<chuckle>resultant amplitude है square root of three squared plus four squared plus zero, यानी root of twenty-five, exactly five centimetres.
phase का tangent बराबर है four times one, over three plus zero, यानी four over three, तो phi है लगभग fifty-three degrees.
ध्यान दो क्या हुआ. चूँकि phasors perpendicular थे, वो Pythagoras से जुड़े, और resultant बस three-four-five triangle का hypotenuse है. कोई heavy trigonometry नहीं.
तो answer है five centimetres की amplitude लगभग fifty-three degrees के phase पर, वही classic three-four-five triangle एक oscillation problem के अंदर चुपचाप बैठा हुआ.

sections.subtopic: Reference Circle, Superposition and More SHM Systems
sections.title: Worked example (NEET): a floating cylinder

board_events.text: Only the submerged depth matters
A wooden cylinder floats upright with 16 cm submerged, then is pushed down and released. Find the period. Take $g=9.8$ m/s².
The trap: no mass, density, or area is needed; the period depends only on the submerged depth.
The form $T=2\pi\sqrt{h/g}$ is identical to a simple pendulum of length $h$.
So a floating body and a pendulum of length equal to the submerged depth keep the same time.
Recognise the skeleton and the numbers fall out in one line.

segments.text: A quick N E E T example that tests whether you recognise the floating-body skeleton rather than hunt for extra data.

A wooden cylinder floats upright in water with sixteen centimetres of its length submerged. It is pushed down slightly and released. Find its period of small vertical oscillations, taking g as nine point eight metres per second squared.
Here is the trap. Students hunt for the mass, the density, or the cross-sectional area, and none of them is needed. For a floating body the period depends only on the equilibrium submerged depth.
So substitute directly into two pi root h over g, with h equal to sixteen centimetres, that is zero point one six metres, over nine point eight.
That is two pi times zero point one two seven eight, which comes to about zero point eight zero seconds.
Notice the shape. The formula two pi root h over g is identical in form to a simple pendulum of length h, one of the period-twins we flagged.
<curious>So a floating body and a simple pendulum whose length equals the submerged depth keep exactly the same time. That twin is worth remembering.
The lesson repeats: recognise which skeleton you are looking at, and the numbers fall out in a single line, no missing data required.
एक तेज़ N E E T example जो जाँचता है कि तुम floating-body skeleton पहचानते हो या extra data ढूँढते हो.

एक wooden cylinder पानी में upright तैरता है, इसकी length का sixteen centimetres submerged. इसे थोड़ा नीचे धकेलकर छोड़ा जाता है. small vertical oscillations का period निकालो, g को nine point eight metres per second squared लेते हुए.
यही रहा trap. students mass, density, या cross-sectional area ढूँढते हैं, और इनमें से कोई नहीं चाहिए. floating body के लिए period सिर्फ़ equilibrium submerged depth पर depend करता है.
तो सीधे two pi root h over g में substitute करो, h बराबर sixteen centimetres, यानी zero point one six metres, over nine point eight.
<curious>वो है two pi times zero point one two seven eight, जो बनता है लगभग zero point eight zero seconds.
shape देखो. formula two pi root h over g, length h के simple pendulum के form जैसा ही है, उन्हीं period-twins में से एक जो हमने flag किया.
तो एक floating body और वो simple pendulum जिसकी length submerged depth के बराबर हो, exactly वही time रखते हैं. वो twin याद रखने लायक है.
सीख दोहराती है: पहचानो कि तुम कौन-सा skeleton देख रहे हो, और numbers एक ही line में निकल आते हैं, कोई missing data नहीं चाहिए.

sections.subtopic: Reference Circle, Superposition and More SHM Systems
sections.title: Worked example (JEE Main): mercury in a U-tube

board_events.text: Total column length, and density cancels
The total mercury column is 1.0 m long. Displace it slightly and release. Find the period. Take $g=9.8$ m/s².
Use the total length $L$ of the liquid column, not the length in one arm.
The period is independent of density: mercury, water, or oil give the same answer for the same column length.
Both the restoring force and the inertia scale with the density, so it cancels.
Column length and $g$ alone set the period.

segments.text: A J E E Main example on the U-tube, and it hides two small traps worth naming.

A U-tube contains mercury; the total length of the mercury column is one point zero metres. The mercury is displaced slightly and released. Find the period, taking g as nine point eight metres per second squared.
Substitute into two pi root L over two g. That is two pi root one over nineteen point six, using the total column length.
Working it out, that is two pi times zero point two two five nine, which comes to about one point four two seconds.
The first trap is the length. L is the total length of the liquid column, not the length in one arm and not the displacement. Get that wrong and every number is off.
<curious>The second point is more surprising. The period is completely independent of the density. Mercury, water, or oil all give the same period for the same column length.
The reason is a clean cancellation. Both the restoring force, from the unbalanced weight, and the inertia, from the moving mass, scale with the density, so the density divides out and disappears.
So the U-tube period is set by the column length and g alone. Recognise the skeleton, use the total length, and ignore whatever liquid is named.
U-tube पर एक J E E Main example, और ये दो छोटे traps छुपाता है जिन्हें नाम देना ज़रूरी है.

एक U-tube में mercury है; mercury column की total length one point zero metres है. mercury को थोड़ा displace करके छोड़ा जाता है. period निकालो, g को nine point eight metres per second squared लेते हुए.
two pi root L over two g में substitute करो. वो है two pi root one over nineteen point six, total column length use करते हुए.
<curious>हल करने पर वो है two pi times zero point two two five nine, जो बनता है लगभग one point four two seconds.
पहला trap length है. L है liquid column की total length, एक arm की length नहीं और displacement नहीं. इसे गलत करो तो हर number बिगड़ जाता है.
दूसरी बात ज़्यादा हैरान करने वाली है. period density से पूरी तरह independent है. mercury, water, या oil सब same column length के लिए same period देते हैं.
वजह एक साफ़ cancellation है. restoring force, unbalanced weight से, और inertia, moving mass से, दोनों density के साथ scale करते हैं, तो density divide होकर गायब हो जाती है.
तो U-tube period column length और g अकेले से तय होता है. skeleton पहचानो, total length use करो, और जो भी liquid नाम हो उसे ignore करो.

sections.title: Worked example (JEE Advanced): a pendulum clock in summer

board_events.text: A longer rod means a slower clock
A clock keeps perfect time at 20 degrees C. The rod has $\alpha=1.2\times10^{-5}$ per kelvin. At 40 degrees C, does it run fast or slow, and by how much per day?
The rod lengthens, so $T\propto\sqrt{L}$ increases; each tick takes longer, so the clock runs slow.
A temperature rise lengthens the rod and the clock loses time; a drop makes it gain.
This is why precision pendulum clocks use temperature-compensated rods.
Answer: the clock runs slow, losing about 10.4 s per day.

segments.text: A J E E Advanced example on the temperature error of a pendulum clock, a perennial favourite across all three exams.

The clock keeps perfect time at twenty degrees Celsius. The pendulum rod has a linear expansion coefficient alpha of one point two times ten to the minus five per kelvin. In summer the temperature rises to forty degrees. Does the clock run fast or slow, and by how many seconds per day?

Reason about the direction first. The rod lengthens with heat, and since the period goes as the square root of the length, the period increases. A longer period means each tick takes longer than a true second, so the clock runs slow and loses time.

Now the size. The fractional change of period is half alpha delta theta, which is half times one point two times ten to the minus five, times a temperature rise of twenty, giving one point two times ten to the minus four.
Multiply by the number of seconds in a day, eighty-six thousand four hundred. The time lost is one point two times ten to the minus four times that, which is about ten point four seconds per day.
<curious>Fix the sign in your memory. A temperature rise lengthens the rod and the clock loses time; a temperature drop shortens it and the clock gains. Warm equals slow.
This is precisely why precision pendulum clocks use temperature-compensated rods, engineered so the effective length barely changes as the seasons turn.
So the answer: the clock runs slow, losing about ten point four seconds per day, and now you know both the direction and the size from one short calculation.
pendulum clock की temperature error पर एक J E E Advanced example, तीनों exams में एक सदाबहार favourite.

clock twenty degrees Celsius पर perfect time रखता है. pendulum rod का linear expansion coefficient alpha है one point two times ten to the minus five per kelvin. गर्मी में temperature forty degrees तक बढ़ती है. clock fast चलता है या slow, और कितने seconds per day?

पहले direction पर reason करो. rod गर्मी से लंबा होता है, और चूँकि period length के square root पर जाता है, period बढ़ता है. लंबा period मतलब हर tick एक true second से ज़्यादा लेता है, तो clock slow चलता है और time खोता है.

<curious>अब size. period का fractional change है half alpha delta theta, यानी half times one point two times ten to the minus five, times twenty का temperature rise, जो देता है one point two times ten to the minus four.
एक दिन के seconds की संख्या से multiply करो, eighty-six thousand four hundred. खोया time है one point two times ten to the minus four times वो, यानी लगभग ten point four seconds per day.
sign दिमाग़ में fix करो. temperature rise rod को लंबा करती है और clock time खोता है; temperature drop इसे छोटा करती है और clock time पाता है. warm बराबर slow.
ठीक इसीलिए precision pendulum clocks temperature-compensated rods use करते हैं, ऐसे बने कि मौसम बदलने पर effective length मुश्किल से बदले.
तो answer: clock slow चलता है, लगभग ten point four seconds per day खोता हुआ, और अब तुम एक छोटे calculation से direction और size दोनों जानते हो.

sections.title: Common pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Five traps in the closing subtopic
Do not add SHM amplitudes arithmetically; use the phasor formula, so the resultant lies between $|A_1-A_2|$ and $A_1+A_2$.
In the U-tube formula, $L$ is the total length of the liquid column, not one arm and not the displacement.
For a floating body use the equilibrium submerged depth $h$, not the total length of the object.
The reference-circle speed is constant, but the shadow's SHM speed is not: fast at the centre, zero at the ends.
Temperature sign: a rise lengthens the rod, raises the period, and the clock runs slow; a drop makes it run fast.
For any unfamiliar system, run the recipe: displace, find the restoring force, shape it into $\ddot{x}=-\omega^2 x$, read $\omega$.

segments.text: Let us close this subtopic with the five traps that catch students on the reference circle and the standard systems.

First, never add S H M amplitudes arithmetically regardless of phase. Two motions of amplitude three and four give a resultant somewhere between one and seven, depending on the phase difference, so always use the phasor formula.
Second, in the U-tube formula the L is the total length of the liquid column, not the length in one arm, and certainly not the displacement. That single mislabel wrecks the answer.
Third, for a floating body use the equilibrium submerged depth, not the total length of the object. The period only cares how deep it sits at rest.
Fourth, keep the reference-circle picture honest. The bead's circular speed is constant, but the shadow's S H M speed is not: it is fast at the centre and zero at the ends.
<whisper>Fifth, get the temperature sign right. A rise lengthens the rod, raises the period, and the clock runs slow; a drop shortens it and the clock runs fast. Warm equals slow.

And the master pro-tip that ties the whole chapter together: for any unfamiliar oscillating system, do not hunt for a memorised formula. Displace it, find the restoring force, shape the result into acceleration equals minus omega squared x, and read omega straight off.
<chuckle>Keep the period-twins on a sticky note: two pi root L over g, two pi root h over g, two pi root R over g. Pendulum, float, planet, same skeleton every time.
चलो इस subtopic को उन पाँच traps से बंद करें जो students को reference circle और standard systems पर पकड़ते हैं.

पहला, S H M amplitudes को phase की परवाह किए बिना arithmetically कभी मत जोड़ो. amplitude three और four की दो motions एक resultant देती हैं one और seven के बीच कहीं, phase difference के हिसाब से, तो हमेशा phasor formula use करो.
दूसरा, U-tube formula में L है liquid column की total length, एक arm की length नहीं, और displacement तो बिलकुल नहीं. वो एक mislabel answer बिगाड़ देता है.
तीसरा, floating body के लिए equilibrium submerged depth use करो, object की total length नहीं. period को सिर्फ़ इससे मतलब है कि वो rest पर कितना गहरा बैठता है.
<whisper>चौथा, reference-circle picture ईमानदार रखो. bead की circular speed constant है, पर shadow की S H M speed नहीं: वो centre पर fast और ends पर zero है.
पाँचवाँ, temperature sign सही करो. rise rod को लंबा करती है, period बढ़ाती है, और clock slow चलता है; drop इसे छोटा करती है और clock fast चलता है. warm बराबर slow.

और master pro-tip जो पूरे chapter को जोड़ता है: किसी भी अनजान oscillating system के लिए memorised formula मत ढूँढो. उसे displace करो, restoring force ढूँढो, result को acceleration बराबर minus omega squared x में shape करो, और omega सीधे पढ़ लो.
<chuckle>period-twins sticky note पर रखो: two pi root L over g, two pi root h over g, two pi root R over g. pendulum, float, planet, हर बार वही skeleton.

sections.title: Formula recap: the whole chapter on one board

board_events.text: Every key relation of Oscillations

board_events.latex: \text{Damped: } A\propto e^{-bt/2m},\ E\propto e^{-bt/m};\ \ Q=\tfrac{m\omega_0}{b},\ N\approx\tfrac{Q}{2\pi}

segments.text: Here is the whole chapter distilled onto a single board. Use it as a last-minute sweep before an exam.
Kinematics first. Acceleration is minus omega squared x. Velocity is plus or minus omega root A squared minus x squared. Maximum speed is A omega, and maximum acceleration is A omega squared.
Energy next. The total is one half k A squared. Kinetic equals potential at x equal to A over root two. And both kinetic and potential energy oscillate at twice the frequency.

The two workhorses. The pendulum period is two pi root L over g; the spring period is two pi root m over k. For combinations, find the effective constant: add reciprocals in series, add constants in parallel.

Damping. Amplitude decays as e to the minus b t over two m, and energy twice as fast, as e to the minus b t over m. The quality factor is m omega-nought over b, and the oscillator rings for about Q over two pi cycles.
Forced motion. Resonance sits at the driving frequency near omega-nought, and the resonant amplitude is about F-nought over b omega-nought, capped by damping.
Superposition. Two collinear phasors add by the law of cosines: A is the root of A-one squared plus A-two squared plus twice A-one A-two cosine delta.
And the standard systems, sharing one skeleton: two pi root L over two g for the U-tube, two pi root h over g for a float, and two pi root R over g for the Earth tunnel.
ये रहा पूरा chapter एक ही board पर निचोड़ा हुआ. इसे exam से पहले last-minute sweep की तरह use करो.
पहले kinematics. acceleration है minus omega squared x. velocity है plus या minus omega root A squared minus x squared. maximum speed है A omega, और maximum acceleration है A omega squared.
अब energy. total है one half k A squared. kinetic बराबर potential x बराबर A over root two पर. और kinetic और potential energy दोनों frequency की दुगुनी पर oscillate करती हैं.

दो workhorses. pendulum period है two pi root L over g; spring period है two pi root m over k. combinations के लिए effective constant निकालो: series में reciprocals जोड़ो, parallel में constants जोड़ो.

damping. amplitude e to the minus b t over two m की तरह decay होती है, और energy दुगुनी तेज़, e to the minus b t over m की तरह. quality factor है m omega-nought over b, और oscillator लगभग Q over two pi cycles ring करता है.
forced motion. resonance driving frequency पर omega-nought के पास बैठती है, और resonant amplitude लगभग F-nought over b omega-nought है, damping से capped.
superposition. दो collinear phasors law of cosines से जुड़ते हैं: A है root of A-one squared plus A-two squared plus twice A-one A-two cosine delta.
और standard systems, एक skeleton share करते: U-tube के लिए two pi root L over two g, float के लिए two pi root h over g, और Earth tunnel के लिए two pi root R over g.

sections.title: Cheat sheet: the memory hooks

board_events.text: Hooks to carry into the exam hall
MAX at MEAN: speed is maximum at the mean, acceleration at the extremes; and $a$ opposes $x$, always pointing home.
Square the swing: energy follows $A^2$; $K=U$ at $A/\sqrt2$, not $A/2$.
Pendulum feels $g_{\text{eff}}$; the spring feels only $k$. Parallel is powerful (stiffer); series is soft.
Resonance is matching rhythm; energy fades twice as fast as amplitude; a high-$Q$ system rings about $Q/2\pi$ times.
One test rules them all: a motion is SHM exactly when $\ddot{x}=-\omega^2 x$; find that line and the period falls out.
Carry these hooks and the whole Oscillations chapter stays at your fingertips.

segments.text: And finally, the cheat sheet: not formulas this time, but the memory hooks that let you reconstruct them under pressure.

First, MAX at MEAN. Speed is maximum at the mean position, acceleration is maximum at the extremes, and acceleration always opposes displacement, always pointing home. That one hook carries the whole of kinematics.
Second, square the swing. Energy follows the square of the amplitude, and kinetic equals potential not at A over two but out at A over root two. Whenever amplitude changes, square the ratio.
Third, the allegiances. The pendulum feels effective gravity; the spring feels only its stiffness k. And for combinations, parallel is powerful, meaning stiffer, while series is soft.
Fourth, the damping trio. Resonance is a matching of rhythm; energy fades twice as fast as amplitude; and a high-quality oscillator rings for about Q over two pi cycles before its energy fades.

<excited>Fifth, and above all, one test rules them all. A motion is simple harmonic exactly when its acceleration equals minus omega squared times its displacement. Find that one line for any system, and the period falls straight out.
Keep the period-twins beside it: root L over g, root h over g, root R over g. Pendulum, float, planet.
Carry these few hooks and the entire Oscillations chapter stays right at your fingertips, from the first swing to the last resonance. That completes the chapter.
और आखिर में, cheat sheet: इस बार formulas नहीं, बल्कि वो memory hooks जो तुम्हें pressure में उन्हें दोबारा बनाने देते हैं.

पहला, MAX at MEAN. speed mean position पर maximum, acceleration extremes पर maximum, और acceleration हमेशा displacement के opposite, हमेशा home की तरफ point करती. वो एक hook पूरी kinematics सँभालता है.
दूसरा, square the swing. energy amplitude के square पर जाती है, और kinetic बराबर potential A over two पर नहीं बल्कि बाहर A over root two पर. जब भी amplitude बदले, ratio को square करो.
तीसरा, allegiances. pendulum effective gravity महसूस करता है; spring सिर्फ़ अपनी stiffness k. और combinations के लिए, parallel powerful है, यानी stiffer, जबकि series soft.
चौथा, damping trio. resonance rhythm का matching है; energy amplitude से दुगुनी तेज़ fade होती है; और high-quality oscillator अपनी energy fade होने से पहले लगभग Q over two pi cycles ring करता है.

<excited>पाँचवाँ, और सबसे बढ़कर, one test rules them all. कोई motion simple harmonic है exactly तब जब इसका acceleration बराबर हो minus omega squared times इसका displacement. किसी भी system के लिए वो एक line ढूँढो, और period सीधे निकल आता है.
period-twins इसके साथ रखो: root L over g, root h over g, root R over g. pendulum, float, planet.
इन थोड़े hooks को साथ रखो और पूरा Oscillations chapter तुम्हारी उँगलियों पर रहता है, पहली swing से आखिरी resonance तक. इसी के साथ chapter पूरा हुआ.
